the-fool.name: The Fool
the-fool.imageAlt: The Fool: a young traveler in bright clothes steps toward a cliff edge under a white sun, carrying a small bag and a white rose, with a small white dog at his heels.
the-fool.summary: The Fool is card 0 of the Major Arcana and stands for new beginnings, spontaneity and trust. Upright, it means stepping into the unknown with an open mind, often before every detail is settled. Reversed, it warns of recklessness, naivety or holding back from a fresh start out of fear.
the-fool.upright: Upright, The Fool marks the start of a journey. Something new is calling, and the card encourages you to answer it with curiosity rather than a full plan. It favors openness, a light attitude and a willingness to learn as you go. The risk is real, but so is the reward of beginning.
the-fool.reversed: Reversed, The Fool points to a beginning that has gone wrong or never happened. It can mean acting without thinking, ignoring obvious warnings or chasing novelty for its own sake. It can also mean the opposite: staying stuck because the first step feels too uncertain.

upright.short: A leap of faith shaped where you are now. You started something without knowing exactly how it would turn out.

reversed.short: An impulsive choice or a missed opportunity in the past still has consequences you are dealing with.

upright.short: You are at a starting line. This is a good moment to try something new and let the plan form along the way.

reversed.short: You may be rushing ahead without looking, or holding back from a start you actually want. Check which.

upright.short: A fresh start is coming. Stay open to an unexpected offer, trip or idea that does not fit your usual path.

reversed.short: A risk lies ahead that is worth thinking through. Slow down before committing so excitement does not outrun judgment.

the-magician.name: The Magician
the-magician.imageAlt: The Magician: a figure in a red robe raises a wand to the sky and points to the earth, with a cup, sword, pentacle and wand on the table before him and an infinity sign above his head.
the-magician.summary: The Magician is card I of the Major Arcana and represents skill, willpower and turning ideas into action. Upright, it says you already have the tools you need and should use them with focus. Reversed, it points to scattered effort, untapped talent or someone using charm to manipulate.
the-magician.upright: Upright, The Magician is about capability. The four suit symbols on his table show that every resource is within reach: passion, feeling, thought and material means. The card asks you to concentrate your will and act. Ideas become real here because someone decides to make them real.
the-magician.reversed: Reversed, The Magician suggests that talent is going to waste or being misused. Energy may be spread across too many projects, or confidence may be missing. It can also flag a person, possibly yourself, who uses persuasion to mislead rather than to build.

upright.short: You made something happen through your own skill and determination, and that achievement is a foundation you can build on.

reversed.short: Past plans stalled because effort was scattered, or someone persuaded you of something that turned out to be untrue.

upright.short: You have what you need right now. Pick one goal, gather your resources and act with intention.

reversed.short: You are capable but unfocused. Cut back to one priority, and watch for anyone whose promises sound too polished.

upright.short: An opportunity is coming to put your abilities to work. You will be in a strong position to shape the outcome.

reversed.short: Be careful of plans that depend on appearances. Unless effort is focused, a promising idea may stay just an idea.

the-high-priestess.name: The High Priestess
the-high-priestess.imageAlt: The High Priestess: a woman in blue robes sits between a black pillar marked B and a white pillar marked J, holding a scroll, with a crescent moon at her feet and a veil of pomegranates behind her.
the-high-priestess.summary: The High Priestess is card II of the Major Arcana and stands for intuition, hidden knowledge and the inner voice. Upright, it asks you to pause, listen and trust what you sense beneath the surface. Reversed, it suggests ignored instincts, secrets or a disconnect from your inner life.
the-high-priestess.upright: Upright, The High Priestess favors quiet understanding over action. Not everything can be learned from facts; some answers come from patience, dreams and gut feeling. The card suggests that information is still hidden, and that waiting and observing will reveal more than pushing for clarity.
the-high-priestess.reversed: Reversed, The High Priestess points to a gap between what you know inside and what you are doing. You may be overriding your instincts, relying too heavily on other people's opinions, or keeping something hidden that wants to come out.

upright.short: A quiet instinct guided you well before, even when you could not explain it. That trust in yourself is still useful.

reversed.short: In the past you ignored an inner warning, or something was kept from you, and the effects are still unfolding.

upright.short: Not everything is visible yet. Hold back from big moves and pay attention to your intuition and dreams.

reversed.short: You are tuning out your own instincts. Make time for quiet, and ask what you already know but have not admitted.

upright.short: Insight is on its way. A hidden detail will surface, or your intuition will point clearly toward the right choice.

reversed.short: A secret may come to light. Rely on your own judgment rather than on gossip or other people's certainty.

the-empress.name: The Empress
the-empress.imageAlt: The Empress: a crowned woman rests on cushions in a field of ripening wheat, holding a scepter, beside a heart-shaped shield bearing the symbol of Venus, with a forest and waterfall behind her.
the-empress.summary: The Empress is card III of the Major Arcana and represents abundance, nurturing and creativity. Upright, it signals growth, comfort and caring for yourself and others, often in relationships, family or creative work. Reversed, it points to neglect, smothering, creative block or dependence on others for security.
the-empress.upright: Upright, The Empress brings growth and plenty. It is a card of tending things so they flourish: a home, a project, a relationship, a body. It encourages pleasure in ordinary comforts and patience with natural timing. Whatever you nurture now is likely to bear fruit.
the-empress.reversed: Reversed, The Empress shows care out of balance. You may be giving so much to others that you run empty, or holding on so tightly that others feel crowded. It can also mean a dry spell in creativity or a lack of support at home.

upright.short: A period of care, comfort or creative growth gave you a solid base. Something you nurtured then is still growing.

reversed.short: Past neglect, overprotection or a lack of nurturing left gaps that you may still be filling.

upright.short: This is a fertile time. Look after yourself and the things you are growing, and let them develop at their own pace.

reversed.short: You are running on empty. Refill your own reserves before giving more, and loosen your grip on what you protect.

upright.short: Growth and abundance lie ahead: a creative breakthrough, a more comfortable home or a relationship that deepens.

reversed.short: Watch for burnout or overdependence. Build security that does not rest entirely on one person or one source.

the-emperor.name: The Emperor
the-emperor.imageAlt: The Emperor: a bearded ruler in red robes and armor sits on a stone throne carved with ram heads, holding an ankh scepter and an orb, in front of bare mountains.
the-emperor.summary: The Emperor is card IV of the Major Arcana and represents structure, authority and stability. Upright, it calls for discipline, clear rules and taking responsibility, often through leadership or a father figure. Reversed, it warns of rigidity, control, abuse of power or a lack of structure where some is needed.
the-emperor.upright: Upright, The Emperor brings order. It suggests building firm foundations, setting boundaries and making decisions with a cool head. It often represents a protective figure or your own capacity to lead. Success comes from planning, consistency and keeping your word.
the-emperor.reversed: Reversed, The Emperor shows structure turned sour. Rules may have become a cage, or someone may be controlling rather than leading. The opposite is possible too: chaos where a plan and some self-discipline would help.

upright.short: Strong structure or a steady authority figure gave you stability. The discipline you learned then still supports you.

reversed.short: A controlling authority or an overly rigid situation in the past shaped how you respond to rules today.

upright.short: Take charge. Set clear goals, organize your resources and make the decisions others are waiting for.

reversed.short: There is either too much control or too little. Check whether you need to loosen your grip or finally put some order in place.

upright.short: Stability is coming through effort and planning. You may step into a leadership role or secure a firm position.

reversed.short: Be wary of a power struggle ahead. Flexibility will serve you better than insisting on being in charge.

the-hierophant.name: The Hierophant
the-hierophant.imageAlt: The Hierophant: a religious figure in red robes and a triple crown sits between two gray pillars, raising a hand in blessing, with two crossed keys at his feet and two followers kneeling before him.
the-hierophant.summary: The Hierophant is card V of the Major Arcana and represents tradition, shared beliefs and learning from established institutions. Upright, it favors convention, mentors, ceremonies and doing things the proven way. Reversed, it suggests questioning rules, breaking with tradition or feeling constrained by expectations that no longer fit.
the-hierophant.upright: Upright, The Hierophant points to the value of what has been passed down. It can mean formal study, a teacher or mentor, a religious or cultural practice, or a commitment such as marriage. The card suggests that working within a recognized system is the right move for now.
the-hierophant.reversed: Reversed, The Hierophant challenges convention. You may feel boxed in by family, school, workplace or faith, or ready to find your own way of doing things. It can also warn against blind obedience to any authority.

upright.short: Tradition, education or a trusted mentor shaped your values. Those lessons still guide your choices.

reversed.short: In the past you broke away from, or felt limited by, a group, belief or set of rules.

upright.short: Lean on proven methods and experienced people. Formal learning or a structured path will serve you well now.

reversed.short: You are questioning the rules. Decide which traditions still have value for you and which you are ready to leave.

upright.short: A mentor, institution or ceremony will play a part in what comes next, perhaps a course, a commitment or a new community.

reversed.short: Expect to test some conventions. Your own path may depart from what others expect of you.

the-lovers.name: The Lovers
the-lovers.imageAlt: The Lovers: a naked man and woman stand in a garden beneath a winged angel in the sun, with a tree of flames behind the man and a fruit tree with a serpent behind the woman.
the-lovers.summary: The Lovers is card VI of the Major Arcana and represents love, union and meaningful choices. Upright, it points to a close relationship, harmony and decisions made in line with your values. Reversed, it signals imbalance in a partnership, conflicting values or a choice you are avoiding.
the-lovers.upright: Upright, The Lovers celebrates connection. It can describe a romantic partnership, but its deeper meaning is choice: committing to something or someone because it truly reflects who you are. The card asks for honesty with yourself and openness with the other person.
the-lovers.reversed: Reversed, The Lovers shows connection under strain. Partners may want different things, communication may be breaking down, or temptation may pull you away from your values. It can also mean postponing a decision because every option feels like a loss.

upright.short: A meaningful relationship or a values-based decision in the past brought you to where you stand today.

reversed.short: A past relationship fell out of balance, or a choice went against your values, and it still affects you.

upright.short: A relationship or decision is at the center now. Choose with your heart and your principles together.

reversed.short: Something is out of alignment. Talk openly about what each side really wants before choosing a direction.

upright.short: A deep connection or an important choice is ahead, and it can bring real harmony if you follow your values.

reversed.short: Expect a test of commitment. Clarify your priorities so temptation or doubt does not decide for you.

the-chariot.name: The Chariot
the-chariot.imageAlt: The Chariot: an armored charioteer under a star-covered canopy stands in a stone chariot drawn by one black and one white sphinx, with a walled city behind him.
the-chariot.summary: The Chariot is card VII of the Major Arcana and represents determination, control and victory through effort. Upright, it means moving forward with focus, steering opposing forces in one direction. Reversed, it points to lost direction, scattered energy, aggression or obstacles you are not yet prepared to overcome.
the-chariot.upright: Upright, The Chariot is about winning through will. The two sphinxes pull in different directions, yet the charioteer holds the course without reins. The card says success comes from discipline, confidence and refusing to be distracted. Keep your eyes on the destination.
the-chariot.reversed: Reversed, The Chariot shows momentum slipping. Conflicting goals may be pulling you apart, or frustration may be turning into force. It can also mean pushing ahead before you are ready, or feeling that circumstances are steering you instead of the other way round.

upright.short: A hard-won success in the past proved what your determination can achieve. That confidence carries forward.

reversed.short: Past efforts lost direction or were blocked, and some frustration from that time remains.

upright.short: Push forward. Focus your energy on a single goal and keep competing priorities under control.

reversed.short: You are pulled in different directions. Pause, choose one route and regain control before speeding up.

upright.short: Victory is within reach if you stay disciplined. Expect progress, travel or a decisive win.

reversed.short: An obstacle or power struggle may slow you down. Plan your approach rather than forcing your way through.

strength.name: Strength
strength.imageAlt: Strength: a woman in a white robe with a crown of flowers gently closes the jaws of a lion, with an infinity sign floating above her head against a yellow sky.
strength.summary: Strength is card VIII of the Major Arcana and represents courage, patience and gentle inner power. Upright, it shows mastering fear or anger with calm compassion rather than force. Reversed, it points to self-doubt, low energy, raw emotion taking over or a need to rebuild confidence.
strength.upright: Upright, Strength describes power that does not need to shout. The woman tames the lion with a gentle hand, not a weapon. The card encourages you to meet difficult feelings, people or situations with steady patience. Real resilience is quiet and kind.
strength.reversed: Reversed, Strength suggests the lion is winning. Anxiety, anger or insecurity may be driving your reactions, or your energy may simply be depleted. The card asks you to be gentle with yourself and rebuild your confidence step by step.

upright.short: You came through a hard time with courage and patience. That experience proved your resilience.

reversed.short: Self-doubt or overwhelming emotion in the past held you back, and you may still carry some of that hesitation.

upright.short: Meet the current challenge calmly. Patience and kindness will get further than force right now.

reversed.short: Your confidence is low or emotions are running hot. Rest, steady yourself and respond rather than react.

upright.short: You will find the courage you need. A situation ahead will show how strong you have become.

reversed.short: Expect a test of nerve. Prepare by caring for your energy so fear or frustration does not take the lead.

the-hermit.name: The Hermit
the-hermit.imageAlt: The Hermit: a bearded old man in a gray cloak stands alone on a snowy peak, holding up a lantern containing a six-pointed star and leaning on a tall staff.
the-hermit.summary: The Hermit is card IX of the Major Arcana and represents solitude, reflection and the search for inner truth. Upright, it encourages stepping back from noise to think deeply or seek guidance. Reversed, it warns of isolation, loneliness or withdrawing too far, or of avoiding reflection that is needed.
the-hermit.upright: Upright, The Hermit lights the way inward. It is a time for retreat, study and honest self-examination. The answers you need are less likely to come from the crowd than from quiet thought. The Hermit can also appear as a wise mentor who offers perspective.
the-hermit.reversed: Reversed, The Hermit suggests solitude has tipped into isolation, or that you are avoiding time alone because of what you might find. It can mean feeling cut off from others, or being too busy to ask the important questions.

upright.short: A period of solitude or reflection helped you understand yourself better. Those insights still guide you.

reversed.short: In the past you withdrew from others for too long, or avoided looking inward when you needed to.

upright.short: Step back and think. Time alone, a quiet routine or a trusted mentor will help you find your answer.

reversed.short: You are either too isolated or too distracted. Reconnect with people, or make room for real reflection.

upright.short: A time of inward focus is coming, bringing clarity about what really matters to you.

reversed.short: Guard against cutting yourself off. Seek counsel rather than trying to solve everything alone.

wheel-of-fortune.name: Wheel of Fortune
wheel-of-fortune.imageAlt: Wheel of Fortune: a large wheel marked with letters and alchemical symbols turns in the clouds, with a sphinx on top, a serpent descending, a jackal-headed figure rising and four winged creatures reading books in the corners.
wheel-of-fortune.summary: The Wheel of Fortune is card X of the Major Arcana and represents cycles, change and turning points beyond your control. Upright, it signals luck shifting in your favor and a new phase beginning. Reversed, it points to a downturn, resistance to change or repeating the same patterns.
wheel-of-fortune.upright: Upright, the Wheel of Fortune turns toward something new. Circumstances are moving, often in your favor, and opportunities may appear suddenly. The card reminds you that every situation is temporary. Adapt to the shift and make the most of the momentum.
wheel-of-fortune.reversed: Reversed, the Wheel of Fortune shows a cycle turning down or stuck. Plans may be delayed by events outside your control, or you may be resisting a change that has already begun. Look for the pattern you keep repeating, since that part is within your power.

upright.short: A lucky break or an unexpected turn of events set your current path in motion.

reversed.short: A setback or run of bad luck in the past changed your plans, and you are still adjusting to it.

upright.short: Things are shifting now. Stay flexible and be ready to act when an opening appears.

reversed.short: You may feel stuck in a downturn or a familiar loop. Accept what you cannot control and change what you can.

upright.short: A turning point is ahead, likely bringing a welcome change of fortune.

reversed.short: A temporary setback is possible. Prepare for it, and remember that the wheel will keep turning.

justice.name: Justice
justice.imageAlt: Justice: a crowned figure in red robes sits between two pillars, holding an upright double-edged sword in one hand and balanced scales in the other.
justice.summary: Justice is card XI of the Major Arcana and represents fairness, truth and cause and effect. Upright, it signals balanced decisions, accountability and outcomes that match actions, including legal matters. Reversed, it points to unfairness, dishonesty, avoiding responsibility or a decision that does not hold up to scrutiny.
justice.upright: Upright, Justice weighs things clearly. It asks for honest assessment, fair treatment and owning the consequences of your choices. Contracts, legal questions and important decisions are favored when handled with integrity. What you have put in is what you will get back.
justice.reversed: Reversed, Justice warns that the scales are off. Someone may be acting unfairly, hiding the truth or refusing to take responsibility, and that someone could be you. A legal or formal matter may not go as hoped. Correct the imbalance where you can.

upright.short: A fair decision or an honest reckoning in the past set things right, and you are living with its results.

reversed.short: A past injustice, dishonest act or avoided responsibility still weighs on the present.

upright.short: Weigh the facts and act with integrity. A fair, well-reasoned choice is needed now.

reversed.short: Something is not being handled fairly. Look honestly at your own part and address what has been avoided.

upright.short: A fair outcome is coming. Decisions, contracts or legal matters should resolve according to the facts.

reversed.short: Be careful of biased judgments ahead. Keep records, stay honest and do not count on shortcuts going unnoticed.

the-hanged-man.name: The Hanged Man
the-hanged-man.imageAlt: The Hanged Man: a man hangs upside down by one foot from a living T-shaped tree, hands behind his back, with a calm face and a golden halo around his head.
the-hanged-man.summary: The Hanged Man is card XII of the Major Arcana and represents pause, surrender and seeing things from a new angle. Upright, it suggests waiting, letting go of control and accepting a delay that brings insight. Reversed, it points to stalling, resistance, pointless sacrifice or indecision that has dragged on.
the-hanged-man.upright: Upright, The Hanged Man asks you to stop pushing. Hanging still, he sees the world upside down, and his calm face shows that this is a choice. The card suggests a voluntary pause, a sacrifice made for a larger aim, or a shift in viewpoint that changes everything.
the-hanged-man.reversed: Reversed, The Hanged Man suggests the pause has turned into being stuck. You may be delaying a decision, clinging to a situation that no longer serves you, or giving things up without any real purpose. It is time to act or let go.

upright.short: A period of waiting or a sacrifice in the past gave you a perspective you still rely on.

reversed.short: In the past you stayed stuck or postponed a decision for too long, and you feel the cost of that delay.

upright.short: Pause before acting. Look at the situation from another angle, and accept that some things cannot be rushed.

reversed.short: You are waiting without purpose. Decide what you are holding on to and whether it is worth it.

upright.short: A pause is coming that will change how you see things. Use it to reflect rather than to worry.

reversed.short: Do not let an unresolved choice drift. If nothing changes, the delay will grow longer.

death.name: Death
death.imageAlt: Death: a skeleton in black armor rides a white horse and carries a black banner with a white rose, while a king lies fallen and a bishop, a woman and a child react, with a sun rising between two towers.
death.summary: Death is card XIII of the Major Arcana and represents endings, transformation and clearing space for something new. It rarely means physical death. Upright, it signals a chapter closing for good. Reversed, it points to resisting a necessary ending, stagnation or fear of change.
death.upright: Upright, Death marks the end of a chapter. A job, relationship, habit or belief has run its course, and letting it go makes room for growth. The rising sun on the card shows what follows. The change may be uncomfortable, but it is clean and final.
death.reversed: Reversed, Death shows an ending that is being resisted. Holding on to what is already over keeps you in limbo and drains your energy. The card asks what you are afraid of losing, and whether staying the same is really safer.

upright.short: A decisive ending in the past cleared the way for who you are now.

reversed.short: You held on to something that had ended, and that delay still affects your situation.

upright.short: Something is ending. Let it go fully, and trust that the space it leaves will be filled with something better.

reversed.short: You are resisting a change that has already started. Releasing it will bring relief.

upright.short: A transformation is coming. One chapter will close so that a new one can begin.

reversed.short: An ending ahead may feel hard to accept. Preparing for it now will make the transition easier.

temperance.name: Temperance
temperance.imageAlt: Temperance: a winged angel with one foot on land and one in a pool pours water between two golden cups, with a path leading to a glowing crown on the distant hills.
temperance.summary: Temperance is card XIV of the Major Arcana and represents balance, moderation and patience. Upright, it means blending opposites, finding the middle way and letting things develop at a steady pace. Reversed, it points to excess, imbalance, impatience or conflict between parts of your life that do not fit together.
temperance.upright: Upright, Temperance is the art of mixing well. The angel pours water between two cups without spilling, a picture of calm, careful adjustment. The card favors moderation, cooperation and healing over time. Small, consistent steps will get you further than extremes.
temperance.reversed: Reversed, Temperance warns that something is out of proportion. You may be overdoing work, spending, food or conflict, or trying to rush a process that needs time. Look for where your life has tipped too far one way.

upright.short: A period of balance and healing in the past helped you recover and find your footing.

reversed.short: Excess or imbalance in the past created problems you are still smoothing out.

upright.short: Aim for the middle way. Patience, moderation and compromise will resolve the current situation.

reversed.short: You are running to extremes. Rebalance your routine and stop forcing a result that needs time.

upright.short: Calm and balance lie ahead. A conflict will ease, and things will come together at the right pace.

reversed.short: Watch for overindulgence or haste ahead. Moderation now will prevent a bigger correction later.

the-devil.name: The Devil
the-devil.imageAlt: The Devil: a horned, bat-winged figure squats on a black pedestal, with a naked man and woman loosely chained to it below, both wearing small horns and tails.
the-devil.summary: The Devil is card XV of the Major Arcana and represents attachment, temptation and feeling trapped. Upright, it points to unhealthy habits, materialism or relationships that hold you more than you hold them. Reversed, it signals breaking free, recognizing a pattern or loosening a hold that once felt permanent.
the-devil.upright: Upright, The Devil shows a bond you may not have chosen consciously. It can be a habit, a debt, a toxic relationship or a fixation on status. Look closely at the card: the chains around the two figures are loose. The trap is real, but so is the way out.
the-devil.reversed: Reversed, The Devil signals awareness and release. You are starting to see what has been controlling you and to take your power back. The process may be uncomfortable, and old cravings may return, but the hold is weakening.

upright.short: In the past you were caught in a habit, relationship or pattern that limited you, and it still shapes your choices.

reversed.short: You broke free from something that held you back. That release is the base for your current freedom.

upright.short: Something has a grip on you. Name it honestly, since seeing the chain clearly is the first step to removing it.

reversed.short: You are loosening an old hold. Keep going, and do not let a moment of temptation pull you back.

upright.short: Watch for temptation ahead. An easy shortcut or a new attachment could cost more than it seems.

reversed.short: Freedom is coming. A pattern that has restricted you is about to lose its power.

the-tower.name: The Tower
the-tower.imageAlt: The Tower: lightning strikes a tall stone tower on a rocky peak and knocks off its crown, as flames burst from the windows and two people fall headfirst through the dark sky.
the-tower.summary: The Tower is card XVI of the Major Arcana and represents sudden upheaval, revelation and the collapse of false structures. Upright, it signals unexpected change that clears the ground for something truer. Reversed, it points to avoiding a necessary disruption, a crisis narrowly averted, or change happening slowly from within.
the-tower.upright: Upright, The Tower brings a shock. Something built on weak foundations comes down quickly, whether a plan, belief, relationship or situation. It is rarely comfortable, but it is honest: what falls was not going to last. Once the dust settles, you can rebuild on solid ground.
the-tower.reversed: Reversed, The Tower suggests the upheaval is being held off or happening internally. You may be propping up something that is already cracking, or you may have escaped a crisis by a narrow margin. The lesson remains, even if the collapse does not come.

upright.short: A sudden shake-up in the past tore down something unstable and forced a fresh start that shaped who you are.

reversed.short: You avoided or postponed a necessary upheaval in the past, and the underlying problem may still be there.

upright.short: Expect disruption now. Let what is unstable fall instead of trying to hold it up.

reversed.short: You are holding back an inevitable change. Facing it on your own terms will hurt less than waiting.

upright.short: A sudden change is coming that will clear away what is false and make room for honest rebuilding.

reversed.short: A crisis may be averted, but only if you address the weak points now rather than later.

the-star.name: The Star
the-star.imageAlt: The Star: a naked woman kneels by a pool under one large eight-pointed star and seven smaller ones, pouring water from one jug into the pool and from another onto the land, with a bird in a tree behind her.
the-star.summary: The Star is card XVII of the Major Arcana and represents hope, healing and renewed faith after difficulty. Upright, it signals calm, inspiration and a clear sense of direction returning. Reversed, it points to discouragement, lost faith or disconnection from what once inspired you, usually only for a while.
the-star.upright: Upright, The Star follows the storm. It brings relief, gentle optimism and the sense that things can get better. The woman pours water freely, a picture of generosity and renewal. The card encourages you to trust the future and reconnect with your hopes.
the-star.reversed: Reversed, The Star shows hope running low. Setbacks may have left you tired, cynical or unsure what to believe in. The card does not mean hope is gone, only obscured. Small acts of self-care and time with what you love can bring it back.

upright.short: After a hard time, a period of healing and hope in the past restored your faith in yourself.

reversed.short: A past disappointment shook your faith, and part of you may still be guarded about hoping again.

upright.short: Healing is underway. Trust your direction, rest and let yourself feel hopeful again.

reversed.short: You feel discouraged. Look for one small source of inspiration and build from there.

upright.short: Brighter days are ahead. Expect renewed confidence, inspiration and a sense of peace.

reversed.short: A dip in motivation may come. Protect your hopes by staying close to the people and practices that sustain you.

the-moon.name: The Moon
the-moon.imageAlt: The Moon: a full moon with a face shines between two towers, while a dog and a wolf howl at it and a crayfish crawls out of a pool onto a winding path.
the-moon.summary: The Moon is card XVIII of the Major Arcana and represents illusion, uncertainty and the subconscious. Upright, it warns that things are not as they appear and asks you to move carefully, guided by intuition. Reversed, it points to confusion lifting, fears being faced or a truth coming to light.
the-moon.upright: Upright, The Moon lights the path only partly. Fears, rumors or wishful thinking may be distorting your view, and some facts are still hidden. The card asks for patience and intuition rather than quick conclusions. Pay attention to dreams and to feelings you cannot yet explain.
the-moon.reversed: Reversed, The Moon suggests the fog is starting to clear. Deceptions may be uncovered, and fears that seemed huge may shrink once faced. It can also mean anxiety bubbling up from below. Either way, honesty with yourself helps.

upright.short: A confusing or uncertain period in the past taught you to rely on your intuition.

reversed.short: In the past, fear or deception clouded your judgment, and you are only now seeing what really happened.

upright.short: Things are unclear right now. Avoid big decisions until you have more facts, and trust your instincts.

reversed.short: Clarity is returning. Face the fear or misunderstanding that has been holding you back.

upright.short: A period of uncertainty is ahead. Move slowly, check information and listen to your inner voice.

reversed.short: The truth will come out. A confusing situation is about to make more sense.

the-sun.name: The Sun
the-sun.imageAlt: The Sun: a smiling sun shines over a wall lined with sunflowers, while a naked child with a feather in its hair rides a white horse and holds a large red banner.
the-sun.summary: The Sun is card XIX of the Major Arcana and represents joy, success and clarity. Upright, it is one of the most positive cards in the deck, signaling warmth, confidence and things going well. Reversed, it points to temporary clouds, dimmed enthusiasm or overconfidence, with the brightness still within reach.
the-sun.upright: Upright, The Sun brings light to everything it touches. Plans succeed, relationships feel warm and you see your situation clearly. The child on the horse shows openness and simple delight. The card encourages you to enjoy the moment and share your good fortune.
the-sun.reversed: Reversed, The Sun is still shining, just behind clouds. Joy may feel muted, success may be delayed, or you may be expecting too much too soon. It can also warn against arrogance. The positive outcome is still likely, just less straightforward.

upright.short: A happy, successful time in the past gave you confidence that still warms your present.

reversed.short: A past success did not feel as bright as it should have, or overconfidence led to a stumble.

upright.short: Things are going well. Enjoy it, share it and let your natural confidence lead.

reversed.short: Something is dimming your joy. Adjust your expectations and look for the good that is still there.

upright.short: Success and happiness are coming. Expect clarity, recognition and plenty of warmth.

reversed.short: Good results are on the way but may take longer than hoped. Stay patient and grounded.

judgement.name: Judgement
judgement.imageAlt: Judgement: an angel in the clouds blows a trumpet hung with a banner bearing a cross, while men, women and children rise from open coffins with outstretched arms, mountains in the distance.
judgement.summary: Judgement is card XX of the Major Arcana and represents awakening, reckoning and answering a calling. Upright, it signals a moment to review the past honestly, forgive and rise to a new stage of life. Reversed, it points to self-doubt, harsh self-criticism or ignoring a call to change.
judgement.upright: Upright, Judgement sounds a wake-up call. It is time to take stock of where you have been, accept the lessons and step into a more authentic version of yourself. The card often appears at a turning point where a decision or realization changes your direction for good.
judgement.reversed: Reversed, Judgement suggests the call is being ignored or drowned out by self-doubt. You may be too hard on yourself to move on, or afraid of what change would demand. The card asks for honest review, not punishment.

upright.short: A wake-up moment in the past changed your direction and helped you understand what you are meant to do.

reversed.short: Past regrets or self-judgment still hold you back from fully moving on.

upright.short: You are being called to rise. Review your choices honestly, forgive what needs forgiving and take the next step.

reversed.short: You are judging yourself too harshly or ignoring a clear signal. Listen, and allow yourself to change.

upright.short: A decisive realization is coming that will open a new chapter.

reversed.short: Do not ignore what you already know you need to change. Waiting will only make the reckoning harder.

the-world.name: The World
the-world.imageAlt: The World: a dancing figure wrapped in a purple sash holds two wands inside a large oval laurel wreath, with an angel, an eagle, a bull and a lion in the four corners.
the-world.summary: The World is card XXI and the final card of the Major Arcana. It represents completion, achievement and wholeness. Upright, it signals that a cycle is fulfilled and you can celebrate before the next begins. Reversed, it points to unfinished business, delays or closure that has not yet come.
the-world.upright: Upright, The World closes the circle. A long effort reaches its natural end, bringing satisfaction and a sense that everything has come together. It can also point to travel or a wider view of life. Celebrate what you have done, then prepare for the next journey.
the-world.reversed: Reversed, The World suggests you are close to the finish but not there yet. Loose ends, delays or reluctance to let go may be keeping a chapter open. Look at what still needs finishing, and resist taking shortcuts at the last step.

upright.short: You completed an important cycle in the past, and that achievement gives you a strong base.

reversed.short: Something in the past was left unfinished, and it still waits for closure.

upright.short: You are reaching a milestone. Acknowledge how far you have come and enjoy the sense of completion.

reversed.short: You are nearly done. Tie up the loose ends instead of moving on before you finish.

upright.short: A goal will be fulfilled. Expect completion, recognition and perhaps travel or a broader horizon.

reversed.short: Closure may take longer than expected. Stay with it and finish properly.
